A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EEG-DisGCMAE and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite reformatting, relocation, additions, and removals.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on HBN and EMBARC, alongside ablations, reconstruction visualizations, efficiency measurements, and held-out validation.

after.justification: v2 retains original clinical experiments and adds perturbation tests, SEED emotion-recognition results, subject-dependent/independent evaluations, and connectivity comparisons.

M1.justification: Equation 7 removes GTD from the stated pre-training objective, retaining joint contrastive and reconstruction losses; downstream GTD and the architecture remain. This is a limited revision to the specified objective. Actual implementation changes remain unresolved because v1's pseudocode already omitted that term, while v2's abstract still mentions distillation during both stages.

E1.justification: v2 adds SEED emotion recognition beyond v1's two clinical datasets and four classification tasks (Appendix F, Table 8). It also adds Gaussian-noise and random electrode-loss scenarios (Section 6, Table 5), extending evaluation to a nonclinical domain and corrupted inputs. Very-low-density and HBN-to-EMBARC held-out evaluations already existed.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 removes SVM, AutoGCL, and S2GAE while retaining the other comparators. LSP and G-CRD remain in the relocated distillation comparison. Section 5.3 newly mentions LaBraM, but no corresponding result is identifiable in the tables or figures, so an evaluated LaBraM addition is not established.

E3.justification: Added protocols include subject-dependent/independent evaluation, SEED graphs using differential entropy and coherence, signal perturbations, alternative connectivity measures, and combined-band inputs. Figure 4 also adds quantitative reconstruction assessment. Existing batch sizes, 200/400-epoch budgets, and ten-fold cross-validation remain unchanged. Noise magnitude, electrode-drop rate, and detailed subject-partition procedures for the new tests are unspecified.

E4.justification: v2 adds corruption robustness, subject-generalization and connectivity analyses, an all-band ablation, and reconstruction MSE measurements. Conversely, the GTD-enabled very-low-density rows in v1 Table 8 and pre-training-GTD conditions in v1 Table 10 disappear from v2 Tables 11 and 13. Existing masking, density, kernel, and fine-tuning analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: Both Appendix D.4 sections specify ten-fold cross-validation with ten runs. The shaded masking-sensitivity plots are retained, and v2 introduces no new seed disclosure, uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Its additional tables continue reporting point results.

E6.justification: All 19 shared rows in Table 1 retain identical values. New results include perturbation scores of 83.7% and 84.0% against an unperturbed 86.9%, SEED scores of 93.6% and 84.3% under subject-dependent/independent settings, connectivity and all-band results, and reconstruction MSE values. Removed baseline and pre-training-GTD entries are deleted evidence, not same-setting performance declines.

T1.justification: Equation 7 substantively revises the formal pre-training objective by removing its GTD term. Otherwise, the two assumptions, graph and kernel definitions, and GTD pair-selection rules remain. The omitted standalone pair-indicator equations are still represented in prose and the relocated Algorithm 1; no new proofs or theoretical guarantees appear.

C1.justification: The central unified pre-training and high-to-low-density distillation contributions remain. v2 explicitly claims the first integration of the two pre-training paradigms within graph networks in its related-work discussion and Impact Statement. It no longer states v1's concluding promises of seamless medical-device deployment and ready extension to brain-computer interfacing and epilepsy detection.

C2.justification: v2 attributes perturbation robustness to masked-electrode reconstruction, interprets SEED results as transfer across domains and graph representations, and explains why functional connectivity can outperform physical distance. It also explains the complementary semantic and structural roles of logits and GTD losses. Existing clinical interpretations and electrode-system limitations are substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code link but removes v1 Appendix O's detailed pre-training pseudocode and the RTX 4090 hardware disclosure. Batch sizes, epoch budgets, preprocessing instructions, and architecture configurations remain, partly relocated. These additions and removals materially change the reproduction information supplied; the PDFs do not establish the linked code's contents or availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion concerning CMAE, GRACE, GraphMAE2, LaBraM, and differential-entropy emotion recognition, while removing the AutoGCL and S2GAE references. It explicitly contrasts vision-domain CMAE with its claimed graph-domain integration gap. The broader EEG, graph-learning, and distillation positioning remains.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v2 condenses the abstract and conclusion, simplifies notation-heavy method descriptions, moves the GTD algorithm and an implementation summary into the main text, and reorders experimental subsections. It removes the pre-training listing and notation glossary and updates authorship and conference information.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, with substantial resizing and relocation of existing displays. Figure 1 is relabeled; new Figures 2, 6, and 7 explain pair selection and pre-training. New experimental tables are added, several ablation tables are restructured, and v1's dataset-distribution figure and notation tables are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful robustness, subject-independent, SEED, and connectivity evidence, but removes comparison baselines, pre-training-GTD analyses, and detailed pseudocode. The new tests lack important protocol details, and Figure 2 with Section 3.3 inconsistently assigns (Fz, T8) to both positive and negative pairs. These gains in evaluation scope coexist with losses in reproducibility and explanatory consistency, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
